set to 1 by the player update when the trigger is down and ammo remains; cleared by ProcessPlayerShots

u8[16], bone -> destroyed-zone bit index for obj+0x1318. char_adv00: bone 2 (head) -> 0, bones 3-5 (right arm) -> 1, bones 6-8 (left arm) -> 2, all others 0xFF -- the shift is masked with 0x1F so those land harmlessly on bit 31.
s8[5], difficulty -> starting g_damage_rank: -3, -1, 1, 4, 8. Not clamped on the way in; UpdateDamageRank clamps to [0,15] on its first pass.
Adaptive 0..15 rank. DamageRankModifier indexes g_pBoneDamageByRank[char][bone*0x10 + rank] with it and adds the signed byte to the table damage.
int[2], per player: the bone index this player's shot hit. DispatchHit copies it from (s8)obj+0x190+player before calling ResolveHit.
int[2], per player, written by ResolveHit: 0 = nothing, 1 = damaged and part swapped, 2 = damaged only, 3 = severed, 5 = no effect (the effect table's `2` sentinel). Result 5 scores nothing.
+player*0x98. Added to the 120-point headshot award and then incremented by 10, so consecutive headshots pay 120, 130, 140 ...; any non-head hit zeroes it.
+player*0x98. Hits that scored, for the end-of-stage accuracy grade evt 0x2B reads.
u16[16], bone -> hit-reaction group. Eight groups partitioning the body: 1 head, 2 torso, 3 right arm (bones 3-5), 4 left arm (6-8), 5 pelvis (9), 6 right leg (10-12), 7 left leg (13-15).
15 sound ids for ActorPlayHitVoice: five flesh impacts (BLOOD02/03/04/06, BONE01), then hurt/kill/head voices as (set A, set B) pairs, then two two-entry pools.
Per character type -> per body condition -> a row whose entries at +0x10 are indexed by the last-hit zone (obj+0x1319). Taken only when obj+0x136C & 0x100, which is [open].

Per character type -> per body condition (obj+0x130C) -> u32[8] motion ids indexed by g_bone_reaction_group. Only two distinct rows exist for the humanoids: the ordinary one is head 977, torso 982, r.arm 981, l.arm 979, pelvis 974, r.leg 961, l.leg 960.
f32, stride 0xC, one per ring set. The middle radius; see g_enemy_approach_rings.
f32, stride 0xC, one per ring set. The outer radius; see g_enemy_approach_rings.
Added to g_enemy_approach_steps when the actor starts between the middle and outer rings.
Added on top of g_enemy_approach_steps_mid when the actor starts outside the outer ring, so a distant enemy walks further before it can attack.

u8 per player. An approaching enemy must claim one through TryClaimAttackSlot before it may attack, so only g_max_attackers enemies commit at a time. The holder's index is kept in obj+0x121, and SelectCameraLookAtTarget focuses the camera on whoever holds one.
Set when a claimed attack has actually started; TryClaimAttackSlot short-circuits while it is set.
The camera block's current look-at point (block+0xD8). StepCameraLookAtDamped eases it toward g_camera_lookat_target rather than snapping.
The point the camera *wants* to look at, chosen by SelectCameraLookAtTarget: a single attacking enemy, the midpoint of two, or the cam/ path's own target when no enemies are registered.
The look-at CamEvalPath7 evaluates from the path's target channels, independent of its eye channels -- which is how a path holds the eye still and sweeps the aim.
How many enemies may hold an attack permit at once: 1 or 2.

Four {inner, mid, outer} f32 ring sets copied into g_enemy_approach_rings by the scene reset. 25/38/51 for most characters, 37/48/51 for set 2. No stage script uses evt 0x0E, so these are what every encounter runs on.
10.0f. RegisterForCameraTracking's sort key is the distance from the camera eye times this, as an int.

Four 64-byte curves indexed by the look-at angle error clamped to 0x1FFF and shifted right 7. The scene reset selects curve 1: rate 64 below about 18 degrees, ramping to 16 past 23. A larger value is a SLOWER turn.
Zeroed by SelectCameraLookAtTarget when no enemy is registered; CameraTrackEnemiesTick uses it to choose between the angle-error curve and a flat rate.
Index into g_camera_turn_rate_curves; the scene reset sets 1.
The rate TurnLookAtToward divides by, refreshed every frame.
{u32 distance key; void *actor} pairs, at most 14, radix-sorted nearest-first before the slots are assigned.
How many entries g_camera_candidates holds this frame.

Per character type -> per body condition -> 0x10-byte attack entries: {s16 strike motion; s16 lunge motion; f32 distance; s16 hit frame; s16 player damage motion; u16 cancel mask}. The cancel mask names zones (1 head, 2 right arm, 4 left arm) whose destruction makes the strike whiff; 8 is outside the 3-bit mask and so never cancels.

Per character type -> per body condition -> s32[80]: which attack to use, indexed (rand%10 + (destroyed_zones & 7) * 10). Ten choices per destroyed-zone combination, so a zombie that has lost its head or an arm reaches for a different attack.
+player*0x98. PlayerTakeDamage decrements it by one per strike; the continue screen restores 1 or 2.
+player. Set to 0x5A by PlayerTakeDamage and counted down; a strike is ignored while it is non-zero.
Accumulates rank adjustments -- PlayerTakeDamage subtracts 2 -- and UpdateDamageRank adds it in and clears it on its next pass.
+player*0x98. Set by PlayerTakeDamage so the player entity plays its damage motion, which is stored alongside at g_player_hit_motion.
+player*0x130. The motion the player entity plays when hit, taken from the attack entry's +0x0A.
The wave-field manager: {u32 active count; u32 slot mask; f32 plane_y; u32; void *sources[8]}. Created by class 0x16, filled by class 0x17.
{handler, object size} per wave-source kind, stride 8: 0 travelling (WaveSourceTravellingTick), 1 circular (WaveSourceCircularTick).
0.01f. A circular ripple's amplitude scales by max(0, 1 - r * this), so it dies at 100 units.

Per body condition -> two 0x10-byte entries in the same layout as g_class30_attacks: entry 0 the right hand (bone 5), entry 1 the left (bone 8). +0x08 is the frame of the throw clip on which the weapon leaves the hand -- 48 for conditions 0/1/3, 35 for condition 2.
The projectile's two states: flight (ThrownWeaponFlyToTarget) and deflected (ThrownWeaponDeflected). Sits immediately before g_class30_states.
Which player TryClaimAttackSlot offers a permit to when g_max_attackers is 1. In a one-player game it is 0, so only g_attack_permits[0] is ever handed out.
Set when two players are actually in play. TryClaimAttackSlot's g_max_attackers == 2 branch picks a permit at random when this is set and falls back to the nearer player otherwise.

One float per character type, copied to obj+0x124 by EnemyZombieInit and EnemyThrowerInit. Paired with obj+0x128, which the zombie sets to 3.5 and the thrower to 5.0 (type 0x16) or 4.0 (types 0x17-0x19).

group*9 + member -> the live BreakablePropUpdate object, or 0 once it is destroyed. Stride 9 because the largest breakable group has nine members. The topple test reads it to find the props a member supports.

Per item-set: how many more props of that set must be destroyed before its hidden item drops. PlaceBreakableGroup seeds it with rand()%n + 1, so which break releases the item is random. Groups 6 and 7 both use set 2, so the later placement overwrites the earlier one's countdown.
96 x {s16 x, s16 y, s16 z}, scaled by 0.001, the prop's collision hull. BreakablePropGroundContact transforms all 96 to find which corner a toppling prop lands on.
15 x {s16 x, s16 y, s16 z} in thousandths -- where each shatter fragment starts, relative to the prop.
15 x {s16 rx, s16 ry, s16 rz} in BAMS -- each shatter fragment's initial orientation.
Per class-0x41-type-4 object kind, stride 0xC: {s16 effect_id @+0, s16 effect_arg @+2, ..., s16 radius @+8}. PlaceKindedProp copies them into the prop's +0x324/+0x328/+0x124.
Per item kind, stride 0xC: the u16 asset slot the pickup is drawn with. g_item_score_table is the s16 two bytes further into the same record.
Per item kind, stride 0xC: the float height the pickup is released at above the prop that hid it.

Which Training Mode lesson is running (g_GameMode == 2). PlaceBreakableGroup uses it to pick which members of a group become one-shot targets with asset 0x1A0F: lesson 0 takes members 2, 3, 4 and 6; lesson 1 takes 0, 1 and 5; lesson 2 takes 0 and 6; lesson 3 takes the same four as lesson 0.
